title: Agent identity and bee spawning (scent, bee, colony)
description:
## Current direction and delivery order — 2026-10-04

Current outcome summary: hv-3x8.9.1 design. Verbatim evidence: hv-3x8.17. Next implementation: hv-3x8.9.3.

The daemon hosts repository-specific colonies (event loops); a sleeping colony does not poll, launch, retry or reconcile. Bee creates requests in Beads independently. A recipe snapshots chosen request parameters; Colony selects the current formula by harness name to produce the actual invocation. Both use canonical bees.toml for their respective concerns. Bee permits per-request CLI values but no alternate recipe file; Colony's transient overrides change formulas/limits, not recipes. SQLite retains registry and formula/override/dispatch history; each wake re-reads canonical config. Use wake/sleep, tmux-style lazy server startup, explicit registration operations, and optional temporary activation. No min policy, no model-cost inference, no idle auto-expiry. Full details and open issues live in hv-3x8.9.1, not in earlier brainstorming below.

NEXT is hv-3x8.9.3: launch a bee from a manually created spawn bead via a small Colony CLI command. Define that slice's cli.ts interface first, then build its usable runtime path. No daemon, Bee CLI or all-commands skeleton yet. This explicit user sequencing replaces the earlier spec -> rename -> shared -> Bee -> daemon waterfall as a prerequisite for the first slice. The full specification and package alignment remain valuable follow-ups, not required detours before this first vertical proof.

The older claim that every request must already come through a implemented Bee producer does not prohibit the approved manual br fixture. Colony remains the execution consumer, not a bypass around spawn beads. Future producer/shared/spec work must reuse the first slice's proven contract. Existing identity, harness capability scope and user-fork exclusions remain unchanged.

Current repository rules allow product imports through @hive/shared only; no mandatory colony -> bee import is needed by the new recipe/formula boundary. Do not silently implement that older proposed exception. GLOSSARY.md and older docs need subsequent reconciliation to the daemon/colony and recipe/formula vocabulary; their update is tracked rather than falsely claimed here.

## Historical prior scope — superseded where inconsistent above

Give coding agents friendly names for identity attribution in Beads, and build a mechanism for human or agent requesters to ask Colony to run bees across harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Pi). These are planned capabilities, not implemented runtime support.

Current vocabulary follows GLOSSARY.md (refined in hv-yan, landed at 882ab2d). Identity identifies a human or agent; best-effort agent attributes describe execution. Owner is the accountable human, distinct from Assignee and Actor. A bee is a running agent, not its request. AFK (away-from-keyboard) work after human-agent planning is the intended default bee mode; HITL (human-in-the-loop) work involves ongoing human participation. This is a terminology alignment, not a new scheduling policy or lifecycle enum.

Three orthogonal parts, sharing only a contract in @hive/shared:
- scent: identity plugins for harnesses (Claude/Codex SessionStart hooks, Pi extension). Reads harness event/context and inherited env; mints a friendly name when no identity is supplied; exports BD_ACTOR (friendly name), BR_HARNESS, BR_MODEL, BR_AGENT_NAME where the harness allows env injection; injects identity into the system prompt/context.
- bee: module + thin CLI. `bee spawn <kind> <task-id>...` creates a spawn bead; `bee status <spawn-id>` reads it. Bee kinds live in a repo-root bees.toml.
- colony: one system-wide daemon (renamed from ghost) that watches spawn beads, launches harness CLIs with identity env, supports restarting execution and stopping running bees as determined by the pending lifecycle design. Only allowed cross-package import: colony -> bee.
An agent can have an identity without being a bee, and a bee is attributed through its inherited env even without scent.

Recorded design inputs (full rationale in the transcript record child bead). The behaviors below come from earlier decisions; final bee lifecycle states, transitions and outcome/event names remain work for hv-3x8.9.1 and hv-3x8.12. The retired term "reap" is not a current domain operation or agreed enum value:
- Friendly name: 3-word adjective-adjective-noun, deterministic from session id for sessions started directly; minted at admission for bees. Model/effort are best-effort agent attributes, separate from identity.
- Identity resolution in scent is lifecycle-aware: sessions started directly mint from the actual session key; harness subagents use a distinct harness-provided agent key; supplied bee identity is adopted and retained across respawns. Clear/new replaces owned session bindings and prompt state, resume restores the target session identity, and compact retains it. A changed session ID alone does not identify a separately launched agent or the requester of a bee; Hive does not add an agent parent-child hierarchy.
- A spawn bead records a request for a bee to work on specified task beads (linked with related deps); it is distinct from the running bee and from the work itself. One request may reference several task beads. Its Requester is the human or agent identity credited with requesting it, not a parent or lifecycle owner. Labels: system, bee, agent:<kind>. br label filters are exact-match, so system:bee would NOT be hidden by --exclude-label system (verified); ordinary agent work already excludes `system` and must ignore system beads.
- bees.toml `users = [...]` is a configurable list of human names (e.g. ct); `bee spawn` fails loudly if any task is assigned to one.
- No single-instance lock for colony.
- Attribution fields: BR_HARNESS=<harness> (e.g. claude) and BR_AGENT_NAME=<bee kind> (e.g. scout), never combined.
- Launch rule: all linked tasks must be ready. A bad DAG is a mistake to fix, not to work around; blocked tasks are allowed at spawn time (deferring a DAG is essential).
- All bee requests go through the bee tool and Colony; no direct subprocess launch path. A requesting agent waiting for requested work is informed via `bee status`, not protected from scheduling waits. This does not describe a parent-child relationship or prohibit harness subagents.
- The earlier design calls for closing a spawn bead to end its request and stop any running bee (allowing interactive TUI bees later). Closed linked tasks count as satisfied: the launch rule applies to the open ones, and Colony closes a request without launching only when all its tasks are closed. A bee whose task claim fails closes its own spawn bead (encoded in the bee policy prompt). Crashes respawn up to max_retries; then colony closes the spawn bead and forcefully returns the bee's claimed tasks to open, as it does after ending a request with unfinished claimed work. colony logs to its own log, not the bead, and emits tracked events for lifecycle actions (likely JSONL).
- colony restarts are likely (e.g. upgrades): bees run detached and survive them; colony recovers from tracked pids and/or a scan of spawn beads.
- Harness subagent definitions (.codex/agents, .pi/agents, agents:sync) are dropped in favour of bees, not regenerated from bees.toml. scripts/beads-loop.ts is temporary and not a design constraint.
- Supersedes the actor policy from hv-ri0 (actor = harness name).

Ordering: spikes and GLOSSARY.md first; then the colony design (hv-3x8.9.1) and the spec (hv-3x8.12), which is the living reference for all later work; then rename, shared contract, scent, bee, colony, retirement.

## Current attribution decision — ct, 2026-10-03

Claude Code harness subagents (Agent/Task) are supported in the planned identity system through the same explicit-attribution approach as Codex. This supersedes the brief exclusion recorded earlier in this discussion.

- Pi: process environment plus stable composable identity in the system prompt on each run.
- Primary Claude Code sessions: SessionStart environment exports plus identity context.
- Codex sessions started directly, Codex harness subagents and Claude Code harness subagents: identity context with explicit `br --actor <own-friendly-name>` on every tracker mutation. Share the explicit-attribution guidance; keep event parsing and context delivery in the harness-specific adapters.
- Each harness subagent uses its distinct agent_id; the shared parent/root session_id supplied by the harness cannot distinguish separate subagents. Preserve the invoking agent's identity and shared environment. An explicit subagent actor overrides inherited BD_ACTOR for that command; do not rewrite the session-wide environment file for a harness subagent.
- Separately launched CLI processes, including colony bees, retain launcher-provided environment support. Identity attribution support for harness subagents does not make them colony-managed spawn beads.

The final policy is agreed here; end-to-end harness subagent attribution is an implementation acceptance criterion, not a completed runtime result of the original spike. The agreed MVP lifecycle boundary is recorded in docs/agent-identity-scope.md: clear/new, resume and compact are supported; user forks are excluded.

## MVP scope and harness conformance

MVP supports start, clear/new, resume, compact and harness-subagent attribution. User fork-in-session and new-fork flows, cache-preserving identity migration and generic GUI support are intentionally excluded. Harness subagents remain in scope even when their harness internally copies history.

References: docs/agent-identity-scope.md and docs/harness-capabilities.md, landed under hv-3x8.15 on main at 2b94294. The capability contract separates versioned upstream evidence from implemented Hive support and defines reusable acceptance cases for future adapters; no runtime capability framework is required.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All child beads closed
- [ ] A Claude, Codex and Pi session started directly each records its agent's friendly name as actor on br mutations (Codex via --actor guidance)
- [ ] `bee spawn` + colony run a bee end to end and attribute its br mutations to its minted identity
- [ ] scripts/beads-loop.ts and harness subagent definition sync are removed
notes:
Design conversation recorded verbatim in hv-3x8.11 (closed record; read with br show hv-3x8.11). Second-opinion reviews by gpt-6-astra are summarised there in the assistant turns.
Aligned with hv-3x8.11 turns 3, 7, 8, 10 (claude audit): added users refusal, claim-fail/reap rules, likely colony restarts, multi-task spawns, no regenerated subagents. Open questions for ct: (1) turn 10 '3. yes i'm fine with this lock for now' answers the pool-deadlock row of turn 9, so it probably means the deadlock, not a two-colony lockfile; confirm whether colony needs a single-instance lock. (2) turn 2: ct suggested the alias under the harness field (claude:scout); the assistant proposed BR_AGENT_NAME=scout with BR_HARNESS separate and ct never confirmed. (3) Multi-task spawns: if one of several tasks is closed before launch, or its claim fails, should the whole spawn bead close?
Resolved by ct after the alignment review: (1) no single-instance lock for colony; (2) BR_AGENT_NAME=<bee kind> with BR_HARNESS=<harness>, not claude:scout; (3) a closed linked task is satisfied, not blocking, so colony must allow it; a linked task blocked after spawn is left unhandled for now (future notification hooks). Still open: a claim failing on only one of several tasks.
ct: outcome labels on closed spawn beads (outcome:exhausted|reaped|unlaunched), colony-only, so bee status reports accurately. Supersedes the earlier exclusion of outcome labels for this narrow use; UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md needs updating (respawn budget -> max_retries, closed not blocked, outcome labels).
hv-3x8.2 identity-hook spike design findings (Claude 2.1.287, Codex 0.160.0, Pi 1.0.0; full matrix + captured samples on child):

- The current HIVE_AGENT_SESSION mismatch rule is broader than nested spawning. Claude/Codex clear and Pi new rotate session id; all root forks also rotate it. A same-process clear/new/fork can therefore be misclassified as a nested child. Decide whether HIVE_AGENT_PARENT describes identity ancestry or actual spawning; distinguish transitions from process nesting where the harness exposes reason/previous session. Clear/compact for Claude/Codex were confirmed against installed/version-matched source, not captured live; Pi lifecycle captured live.
- Harness-native subagents are not separate root sessions: Claude SubagentStart.session_id is parent; Codex 0.160.0 session_id is the ROOT id across descendants. Both have distinct agent_id; Claude env-file exports are shared by parent/subagent Bash, and SubagentStart has no CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. Codex has no hook-output env channel. Native subagents receive separate actor names through explicit prompt/tool attribution per ct’s final decision below; root SessionStart alone cannot export isolated native-subagent identities. Collaboration Codex DOES fire SubagentStart once registered; earlier negative probe was a missing registration, not a product blind spot. Retiring native definitions does not itself disable native subagent tools.
- Claude SessionStart.model is optional and absent in the actual startup/resume/fork probes even with CLI/settings/env model pins; effort is unavailable at SessionStart. Codex includes resolved model but no effort. Treat metadata as best-effort and do not invent required fallback values. Pi ctx exposes model + thinking, with selection-change events for refresh.
- Pi identity is stable through ordinary per-run prompt composition: each before_agent_start handler appends to the current event.systemPrompt, and subsequent handlers receive the result. ct confirmed this is sufficient, not a prompt-persistence design concern; the installed 1.0.0 runner passed a two-extension, three-run composition probe. Compaction has its own prompt, keeps id and does NOT emit session_start. Pi RPC new/resume/fork emits start twice (double rebind in installed source), so lifecycle handling must be idempotent. Do not generalize RPC duplicate behavior to TUI without evidence.
- Native Codex remains explicit --actor guidance, not dynamic env export. Parent linkage of separately launched nested CLIs from a native Codex parent is incomplete if scent cannot bind/export HIVE_AGENT_SESSION. Production hooks also need an explicit trust-install/launch policy; disposable exec probes required --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, not a flag to silently adopt in colony.
- Version provenance matters: vendored Codex e597169e is older than installed 0.160.0 and lacks fork; matched rust-v0.160.0 commit a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc supersedes it for this spike. Claude default auto-updated to 2.1.288 during review; captures and inspected bundle are pinned 2.1.287, not a claim about 2.1.288.

These are scope findings/policy questions for the spec, not additional work claimed or implemented by this spike. Remaining live-verification limits are explicitly listed on hv-3x8.2; no unsupported capability is silently assumed.
hv-3x8.1 completed database/worktree spike (br 0.7.4 commit 3956ebb; complete exact command ledger and observations on the child; 170 disposable assertions, full check and 262 repository tests passed; independent review cleared).

Recommendation for this epic/spec, NOT an applied policy change: one canonical .beads/beads.db per repository for bee/colony coordination; preserve caller/worktree cwd for code execution. Resolve Honeycomb primary root (not git rev-parse --show-toplevel in a worktree), use explicit --db for colony/bee-owned br calls and pin child BEADS_DB with competing routing env removed. System-wide colony needs explicit per-repo endpoints/registrations and per-spawn persisted DB authority; use subprocess-local args/env/cwd, never the daemon's own cwd or global env to choose a repo.

Evidence warranting departure from cwd-only routing: DB-less upstream worktrees fall back to primary, but Hive post-checkout explicitly creates private worktree DBs. Hive disables auto-import/flush; main-only polling cannot see worktree spawns/claims/closure until JSONL export + commit + merge/reconciliation. Identical task IDs were successfully claimed in both independent DB copies. If ct retains workspace-local queues instead, colony must register/poll each resolved caller DB and explicitly define independent claim/spawn identity domains; main-only polling is not workable.

Required follow-up decision (not implemented or separately claimed): update AGENTS.md/spec plus .husky/beads-sync/prepare/checkout/commit/merge transport policy together. BEADS_DB alone cannot change hooks because their worktree --db wins; worktree Git cannot stage canonical JSONL. IMPORTANT: replacing canonical JSONL with an older worktree snapshot caused sync --merge to tombstone an omitted canonical-only bead (merge deletion), even while retaining independent changes. Reconcile existing DB-only local state and establish coherent merge-base/transport handling; do not blindly copy old snapshots or use routine force/allow-stale. --allow-stale skips startup import, not stale export/semantic conflict guards. Details and limitations on hv-3x8.1. All follow-ups remain for the downstream design/spec; no additional bead was picked up.

## Current attribution decision — ct, 2026-10-03

Native Claude Code Agent/Task subagents are supported in the planned identity system through the same explicit-attribution approach as Codex. This supersedes the brief exclusion recorded earlier in this discussion.

- Pi: process environment plus stable composable identity in the system prompt on each run.
- Primary Claude Code sessions: SessionStart environment exports plus identity context.
- Native Codex sessions/subagents and native Claude Code subagents: identity context with explicit `br --actor <own-friendly-name>` on every tracker mutation. Share the explicit-attribution guidance; keep event parsing and context delivery in the harness-specific adapters.
- Native child identity uses the distinct agent_id; parent/root session_id alone cannot distinguish siblings. Preserve the parent identity and shared environment. An explicit child actor overrides inherited BD_ACTOR for that command; do not rewrite the session-wide environment file for a native child.
- Separately launched CLI processes, including colony bees, retain launcher-provided environment support. Identity attribution support for native subagents does not make them colony-managed spawn beads.

The final policy is agreed here; end-to-end native child attribution is an implementation acceptance criterion, not a completed runtime result of the original spike. Clear/fork ancestry policy remains a separate question.

Support evidence for the explicit route: the original spike observed distinct native agent_id values and shared parent/root session IDs. Claude’s official SubagentStart reference documents additionalContext delivered into the child before its first prompt: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart (checked 2026-10-03; current documentation, not a new pinned-version live capture). Installed br is 0.7.4. Matching beads_rust@3956ebb source reads BD_* environment into a layer (src/config/mod.rs:6020), applies explicit actor in CliOverrides (6157), and pushes the CLI layer after startup/environment layers (6360-6366); --actor therefore overrides inherited BD_ACTOR. No new live Claude/Codex child-attribution probe was run in this correction.

References: docs/agent-identity-scope.md and docs/harness-capabilities.md, authored under hv-3x8.15 in branch codex/harness-capability-docs (pending application-code integration). title: Spike: br database discovery across nested worktrees and BEADS_DB policy
description:
Before bee and colony pin which Beads database a bee uses, establish how br behaves when invoked from nested Git worktrees (honeycomb creates them under .worktrees/ in this repo).

Questions:
- From a nested worktree cwd, which .beads/ does br discover: the worktree's checked-out copy or the main checkout's? Is the SQLite db shared or per worktree, and how does the Husky reconciliation (pre-commit / post-merge / post-checkout) interact?
- If a bee mutates beads from a worktree while colony reads the main checkout, when does each side see the change?
- Does forcing BEADS_DB (br honours the env var and --db) to the canonical git-root database work from a worktree, and what breaks (auto-flush to JSONL, freshness checks, --allow-stale)?
- colony is one system-wide daemon serving many repos (not started per repo): how should it address each repo's database when polling spawn beads and launching bees?
- Recommend a policy: bee caller's cwd vs BEADS_DB always = canonical git root. ct leans to the bee caller's cwd, and is open to a policy change making BEADS_DB always the canonical git root if the spike shows it is needed (hv-3x8.11 turn 7 #5).

Prior evidence: hv-mmk and hv-00n verified two-worktree reconciliation. Use disposable repos/worktrees in $TMPDIR; do not mutate this repo's tracker for experiments.
design: Research-only spike; no product or repo-policy edits. Use isolated HOME/XDG/Git config and disposable repos under TMPDIR. Compare default br discovery/visibility with Hive no-auto-import/no-auto-flush config; run copied reconciliation hooks through real Git lifecycle; test BEADS_DB and --db from nested worktrees, freshness guards and ambient overrides. Record exact reproducible commands, outcomes, recommended bee/colony routing and follow-ups on this bead only. Baseline bun run check passed in task worktree.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Observed discovery and visibility behaviour recorded in notes with the exact commands run
- [x] Recommended BEADS_DB/cwd policy for bees recorded in the epic design or notes
- [x] Any required repo policy change (e.g. AGENTS.md) called out as a follow-up
- [x] Hook-free worktree discovery and upstream manual sync runbook reproduced in a disposable codebase, with comparison to Hive hooks and a supported recommendation
notes:
Aligned with hv-3x8.11 turns 7 #5, 10: added ct's cwd preference and system-wide colony routing question.
## hv-3x8.1 — database discovery and bee/colony routing spike (2026-10-03)

Research completed without product-code or repository-policy changes. All experiments used disposable repositories under TMPDIR; Hive's tracker was not used as an experiment fixture. The implementation deliverable is these findings plus the exact command ledger below. No other task was claimed or implemented.

### Provenance and isolation

Installed br 0.7.4, release commit 3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75; inspected matching vendored source at /Users/ct/dev/vendor/beads_rust@3956ebb. Honeycomb 0.5.0, Git 2.56.0, Bun 1.4.2, Darwin arm64. Consulted installed capabilities/help rather than assuming the older skill reference's version.

Every experiment isolated HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1; removed inherited BEADS*/BR_*/BD_* database/sync settings; set process-local BD_ACTOR=pi; synthetic creates/claims used owner ct. Honeycomb created nested .worktrees/ directories against disposable local bare origins. No raw git worktree lifecycle commands were issued by the experiment harnesses. A/B subprocesses had a 300s cap; C/D had a 45s cap; none timed out.

### Observed discovery: cwd alone is not a stable store selection

- Without hooks, a fresh linked worktree has tracked .beads/config.yaml, metadata.json and issues.jsonl but no ignored SQLite DB. Plain br where --json from both its root and a deep subdirectory resolves the PRIMARY checkout's .beads/beads.db and issues.jsonl. A worktree mutation is immediately visible to main and, with br's default auto_flush=true, exports main's JSONL; worktree JSONL is unchanged. A24–A31.
- Explicit br --db <worktree>/.beads/beads.db --no-auto-import list --json bootstraps a private DB from the worktree JSONL despite the auto-import opt-out. After that, ordinary cwd discovery selects this local DB; filesystem inodes differ. --no-auto-import does not prevent missing-DB recovery. A35–A41.
- These observations assume ordinary .beads discovery, default metadata and no explicit redirect/BEADS_DIR/cache overrides; they are not a claim about every supported br configuration.
- In this repository, Hive's post-checkout hook explicitly targets $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.beads/beads.db. show-toplevel means the current worktree, not Honeycomb's canonical root. The missing-DB helper branch uses --no-auto-import sync --merge --force-jsonl, creating a local DB during honeycomb add. Git traces verified real post-checkout execution. Hive therefore normally has ONE DATABASE PER WORKTREE, despite upstream br's DB-less-worktree fallback. B21–B25, C17.

### Visibility and reconciliation

- Hive config disables both sync.auto_import and sync.auto_flush. A worktree create remains DB-only: neither JSONL nor main's DB sees it. Worktree br sync --merge exports/reconciles only that worktree; main JSONL remained SHA-256-identical and main's DB still lacked the bead. B28–B34.
- The pre-commit Beads step exports/reconciles and stages worktree JSONL; commit carries it. Git merge transports the JSONL to main; post-merge reconciles main's DB, making the change visible even with auto-import disabled. Reverse visibility requires the analogous main export + commit + worktree merge/reconciliation. Hooks reconcile the current checkout; they do not replicate databases or transport branch state themselves. B35–B52.
- A DB-only addition and an independent JSONL-only label edit both survived the pre-commit sync, commit and merge, without forced conflict resolution. B53–B66. ### Explicit canonical BEADS_DB/--db

- BEADS_DB=<canonical>/.beads/beads.db from an initialized worktree selects canonical DB, project config and sibling canonical JSONL. A pinned create is visible immediately to main's DB, not the worktree's private DB. With Hive config, neither JSONL auto-flushes; pinned sync --merge writes ONLY canonical JSONL. C01–C05.
- With vanilla defaults, the same pin auto-flushes canonical JSONL only. Even malformed worktree JSONL is irrelevant to the pinned family's freshness check. D01–D02. No redirect file or redirected_from output was necessary for explicit routing in these fixtures.
- Existing Hive beads-sync supplies its own --db <worktree path>, which wins over inherited BEADS_DB. Giving a bee canonical BEADS_DB therefore DOES NOT switch current hooks to a shared database policy. C06. Furthermore git add <canonical>/.beads/issues.jsonl from a linked worktree fails exit 128, outside repository: canonical export cannot simply be staged by a worktree's current pre-commit. C16.
- Replacing canonical JSONL with an older worktree generation is NOT a safe additive handoff. In C07, sync --merge retained an active pending canonical title update and an active worktree-only addition, but TOMBSTONED the already-exported canonical-only bead omitted by the older JSONL (delete_reason="merge deletion"). Missing-from-JSONL relative to the base is interpreted as deletion. C07/C07b now assert status as well as title; the earlier title-only check missed this and was corrected after review. Do not blindly copy stale worktree JSONL over a shared tracker; coherent base/transport policy is required. This also does not promise conflict-free same-field edits.
- Absolute --db under .beads works from a neutral, nonrepository cwd for main, worktree-local and another unrelated repository. Colony need not have a repo-specific process cwd to route br. C08–C10.
- --db wins over BEADS_DB and legacy aliases. Inherited BD_DB/BD_DATABASE can override BEADS_DB alone; the launch boundary must remove competing database/JSONL/directory/cache overrides, or explicitly route command-owned br calls. C11–C13. Pin the whole workspace family, not an external cache DB with incidental caller config.

### Freshness and --allow-stale

- On a clean default DB, changed CANONICAL JSONL is auto-imported before a pinned read. --allow-stale and --no-auto-import instead return the old DB view. D03–D05. These flags are not worktree-sharing mechanisms.
- Dirty DB plus externally changed JSONL is not an automatic hard refusal in this installed version: startup WARNs "Skipping auto-import", returns exit 0 and the old DB view. Explicit sync --merge reconciled independent pending changes after establishing the common base. D06–D07.
- --allow-stale sync --flush-only still refused loss of a JSONL-only ID: exit 7, CONFIG_ERROR, "Refusing to export stale database that would lose issues". Explicit merge retained it. D08–D09. --allow-stale sync --merge also refused a conflicting title edit: exit 7, CONFIG_ERROR, BothModified. It does not bypass export guards or select a conflict winner. D10.
- Missing beads.base.jsonl with differing DB/JSONL refuses to guess an ancestor (exit 6, SYNC_CONFLICT). E01–E03 explicitly retain this fixture/result: a DB-only seed plus empty JSONL refused merge; initial flush-only followed by merge established agreement and a base. Normal Hive missing-DB bootstrap already explicitly chooses JSONL. Auto-import does not itself advance the three-way merge base: checkpoint agreement with sync --merge when needed. In an earlier retained refinement run, skipping that checkpoint led to BothModified when another JSONL title generation was presented; this is not an argument to force routine sync.
- br's mutation success does not guarantee JSONL publication: Hive intentionally disables it; default auto-flush failures may warn after the DB mutation. Poll the selected DB using br, not issues.jsonl as a live queue. Do not use --allow-stale/--force as a blanket daemon error workaround; surface sync conflicts for reconciliation.

### Recommendation for the epic/spec (not applied)

Recommend ONE CANONICAL TRACKER PER REPOSITORY for bee/colony runtime, while preserving caller/worktree cwd for code execution. Set a bee's BEADS_DB to the absolute canonical .beads/beads.db; use explicit --db for colony/bee-owned br calls. This separates execution location from coordination authority. Canonical here is Honeycomb's primary root (or the Git common-directory equivalent), not git rev-parse --show-toplevel in a worktree.

Why prefer this over ct's cwd-only preference: Hive creates private stores, so a main-only daemon cannot observe a worktree's new spawn, task claims or closure until commit/merge. A parent waiting for its queued child cannot rely on that handoff. Polling every worktree DB can make cwd-local spawning visible, but it still allows independent claims of identical task IDs across stores and duplicates imported spawn records. That alternative is viable only if the spec intentionally defines independent workspace queues and registers/pins each caller's resolved br where database; it is not interchangeable with one repository-wide queue. The evidence justifies recommending canonical authority, not silently changing today's policy.

System-wide colony should maintain explicit repository registrations keyed by canonical root, with that repo's absolute database path and bees.toml/config location. Poll each registered endpoint through a subprocess-scoped br --db <path>, and persist that endpoint with each admitted spawn/bee. Use a separate execution cwd for each bee. Never infer a target from colony's own cwd or set process-global BEADS_DB/chdir across repositories. All br show/ready/claim/status/close calls for a spawn and its tasks must use the same authority. The neutral-cwd, two-repo probes establish routing feasibility; registry implementation, daemon concurrency, recovery and dynamic repository enrollment belong to the downstream design, not this spike.

### Required follow-ups if adopting the recommendation

1. Explicitly approve/document the tracker authority in AGENTS.md and the bee/colony spec: worktree code cwd remains allowed/required; br mutations for runtime tasks use the canonical repo tracker. No policy file was changed by this spike.
2. Revisit .husky/beads-sync and prepare/post-checkout/pre-commit/post-merge integration together, including how canonical JSONL is transported/staged for a worktree commit. Merely exporting BEADS_DB or replacing the helper's DB path is insufficient; it currently creates local stores and stages checkout-local JSONL. C07b demonstrates that replaying an older checkout JSONL over canonical JSONL can tombstone newer canonical records. Do not invent a canonical-db/local-jsonl hybrid or blind snapshot-copy migration without checking br's family/path safety and establishing the correct merge ancestor.
3. Reconcile extant worktree DB-only state before changing authority; setting the env var alone would abandon pending local claims/notes. Define synchronization and semantic-conflict handling without routine force/stale bypasses. Preserve current Hive auto-sync configuration unless a deliberate follow-up changes it.
4. Specify canonical root resolution, repository registration, per-spawn database pinning and environment sanitization at the bee/colony boundary. If ct chooses workspace-local queues instead, require polling registered workspace DBs (not main only) and an explicit task/spawn identity/claim-domain rule.

## 2026-10-03 hook-free follow-up requested by ct

### Conclusion and upstream intent

The per-worktree split observed in the original spike is a consequence of Hive's custom bootstrap helper, not the normal br 0.7.4 worktree workflow. With no Git hooks and no database override, fresh linked worktrees resolve the complete DB/config/JSONL family to the primary checkout. Cwd can remain the code worktree while tracker authority is primary. A main-checkout colony would immediately see new spawns, claims, and closures in this topology, without a commit/merge handoff. This refines the original rationale: worktree-local invisible queues describe today's customized Hive topology, not a general br limitation. Explicit per-repository --db routing for the system-wide daemon remains appropriate, especially with already-initialized stores or inherited overrides.

This is deliberate upstream behavior. Maintainer confirmation on PR #429 (https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/pull/429) explains that discovering the tracked snapshot as a workspace rebuilt a private DB from possibly stale JSONL and split state. The fix routes a linked worktree with no local DB/redirect to primary; existing local DBs and explicit redirects remain supported choices. Matching installed source: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/blob/3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75/src/config/mod.rs#L322-L398.

Hooks themselves are allowed: upstream SYNC_SAFETY.md documents an optional custom flush-and-stage hook. The problem is the specific Hive policy: .husky/beads-sync uses git rev-parse --show-toplevel, then explicit --db <worktree>/.beads/beads.db and, when absent, --no-auto-import sync --merge --force-jsonl. That bootstraps the very private store upstream default discovery avoids. Hive's sync.auto_import=false and sync.auto_flush=false separately replace normal automatic publication/import with manual/hook responsibility.

### Recommended no-hook runbook

Authority: the installed br robot-docs guide, reproduced verbatim in the experiment transcript, plus the README and SYNC_SAFETY.md at the installed release commit. Sources:
- https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/blob/3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75/src/cli/commands/robot_docs.rs
- https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/blob/3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75/README.md
- https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/blob/3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75/docs/SYNC_SAFETY.md

1. Initialize br once in the primary checkout. Keep normal sync.auto_import/auto_flush defaults enabled. Do not initialize or explicitly bootstrap a private database in each linked worktree unless independent workspace trackers are intentional. Verify selection with br where --json.
2. Use br from the code cwd. Mutations normally update SQLite and auto-flush the selected workspace's issues.jsonl; ordinary commands check changed local JSONL and auto-import when safe. Neither phase runs Git or transports branch state.
3. At completion, br close <id> --reason 'Completed: <proof>' --actor <harness> --json, then br sync --flush-only. Stage code and .beads changes explicitly with Git; commit/push remain operator/agent actions. No routine merge, force, or allow-stale flag is required for ordinary export.
4. After Git pull/merge has delivered changed JSONL, inspect br sync --status --json and use br sync --import-only for an explicit import. With default settings an ordinary issue read also performs the safe startup import. Resolve Git conflict markers before importing.
5. Reserve br sync --merge for independently changed DB and JSONL. It requires the saved .beads/beads.base.jsonl and explicit handling of semantic conflicts. Auto-import is not proof that a merge base exists. In this clean imported-clone fixture, sync --merge initially refused missing base (exit 6); an ordinary final flush brought exported DB and JSONL into agreement, then unforced sync --merge established the base before divergence. After a no-auto-flush DB title edit plus a different issue's upstream JSONL title edit, normal startup warned/skipped import, and explicit unforced sync --merge preserved both active issues. This is a controlled checkpoint demonstration, not permission to force an export over arbitrary drift.

Worktree staging caveat: br flush from a linked worktree exports PRIMARY JSONL, while git add .beads there stages that worktree's tracked snapshot. The generic runbook's same-checkout staging example therefore must be applied at the selected tracker workspace root. Our tested no-copy handoff was: commit feature code in its worktree, run br sync --flush-only and git add .beads / git commit at primary, then integrate the feature through normal Git merge. Primary tracker records survived integration. Trying git add <primary>/.beads/issues.jsonl from the linked worktree was refused (exit 128 outside repository). A requirement to package all tracker/code edits into the same branch commit needs a deliberate Git handoff design; the guide does not solve that automatically, and blind snapshot copying is not recommended.

### Observed comparison

- Vanilla defaults + no hooks: nested worktree root, deep subdirectory, second nested worktree and sibling worktree all resolve primary DB/JSONL. A worktree create is immediately visible from primary/other worktrees and exports primary JSONL only; no private DB appears. A claim becomes visible everywhere and a different actor's second claim is refused (exit 4). Closure is visible without Git transport.
- No hooks + Hive's autosync-off config: still one primary DB and immediate visibility, but no automatic JSONL export. Explicit sync --flush-only exports primary JSONL. Thus the config flags do not create separate stores.
- Same fixture + explicitly invoking the unchanged Hive helper once (still no installed/executed Git hooks): it creates a private DB from the older checkout JSONL and subsequent ordinary discovery chooses it. ### Exactly when files and Git dirtiness change

SQLite is ignored runtime state. A task mutation changes the selected DB immediately, but that alone does not dirty Git. JSONL is tracked interchange state.
- Shared-primary with default auto_flush=true: successful task create/claim/notes/close normally exports primary JSONL immediately. If exported bytes differ from the staged/committed version, primary is dirty; the feature's tracked JSONL stays unchanged.
- Shared-primary with auto_flush=false: task changes remain in ignored primary DB and are visible immediately to all callers using that DB. Primary JSONL remains unchanged and canonical Git remains clean until an explicit sync export/checkpoint.
- br sync --flush-only exports the selected DB; if bytes differ, primary becomes dirty. It neither stages nor commits nor pushes. Re-running with no changed bytes need not dirty anything.
- git add stages the file; staged-but-uncommitted changes still fail Honeycomb's porcelain cleanliness check.
- git commit records those bytes and makes the checkout clean (assuming no other edits), but HEAD is now ahead of origin and fresh_canonical still refuses.
- git push publishes the commit; subsequent fetch sees matching origin state and restores readiness if no additional changes arose.
- A successful Git merge or squash integration may change tracked JSONL but records the resulting bytes in its commit. Changing a file as part of a committed checkout update is not inherently Git dirtiness. Conflicted or uncommitted merges are different.
- With no Git hook, Git merge does not update SQLite itself. If incoming committed JSONL changes need to enter the selected DB, a normal br command can auto-import when safe, or use explicit sync --import-only. If the DB has pending independent changes, use the established-base sync --merge procedure from the earlier follow-up; ordinary startup can warn/skip instead of importing.

### Example 1: default auto-flush blocks main during feature work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Task["Task update in feature worktree"] --> Database["Shared primary SQLite changes"]
  Database -- auto flush --> Export["Primary issues.jsonl changes"]
  Export --> Dirty["Main has uncommitted changes"]
  Dirty --> Refused["Default Honeycomb add and finish refuse"]
```

16-case experiment G01-G03: feature code already committed and feature Git clean; br create from that feature produced only M .beads/issues.jsonl in primary. New default add and squash finish both returned exit 10 reason dirty_canonical.

### Example 2: publish tracker, then integrate code

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Changed["Main JSONL differs from commit"] --> Local["Commit tracker: main clean but ahead of origin"]
  Local --> Blocked["Fresh canonical still refuses"]
  Local -- push --> Published["Main clean and published"]
  Published --> Integrated["Honeycomb integrates feature code"]
  Integrated -- close task with auto flush --> DirtyAgain["Main JSONL changes again"]
```

G04-G11: tracker commit cleared main's dirty status but made it one commit ahead; default add and finish returned exit 10 reason non_ff_canonical. Push to disposable origin restored add readiness. Squash finish then integrated the code and preserved the primary's already-published tracker addition, even though the feature branch's committed JSONL snapshot lacked that bead. This is ordinary three-way Git merge behavior: an unchanged older snapshot does not overwrite a change made on the other side. Both sides actually editing the same JSONL line can conflict; this case did not test such a conflict. After the integrated main was pushed, br close from the retained feature worktree exported a closed status to primary JSONL, dirtied main again, and blocked the next default add. Commit+push of completion restored it.

Conceptual Git comparison: common ancestor has task=open; main commits task=in_progress; feature changes only code and retains task=open. Integration keeps task=in_progress plus feature code, rather than treating the feature's older file as a replacement snapshot. Do not manually copy that old snapshot onto primary.

### Example 3: shared live DB with deliberate publication

P01-P05: a separate fixture initialized br once at primary, with sync.auto_import=true and sync.auto_flush=false, and no hook/private worktree bootstrap. Worktree br create updated the shared DB and was immediately visible from primary while both Git roots remained clean. Another default Honeycomb add succeeded. Explicit br sync --flush-only from the worktree then exported primary JSONL and dirtied main; add refused until those bytes were committed and pushed at primary. Thus sharing runtime task authority and scheduling JSONL publication are independent choices.

This revises the preceding blanket recommendation to restore both auto-sync defaults: for Hive's clean-main workflow, shared-primary runtime DB plus deliberate JSONL publication is a candidate to evaluate. Keep automatic import enabled if desired, and coordinate publication/import around concurrent agents and incoming Git state. With auto-flush disabled, pending live DB state is not yet Git-published/backed up through JSONL. A dedicated tracker workspace is another architectural option, but was not implemented or tested here. Existing initialized worktrees still require reconciliation before any authority change.

Current Hive's contrast: its helpers create per-worktree stores and disable both automatic phases. A normal task update changes ignored worktree DB; pre-commit exports/stages local JSONL with the code commit, while post-merge reconciles primary. That lets code and tracker travel through a branch commit and keeps routine worker task updates from dirtying main, but yields separate claim/visibility domains. The helper solves a Git publication problem while introducing a coordination tradeoff; it is not simply forbidden by upstream. No policy has been changed.

### Evidence

16/16 targeted assertions passed. Installed br 0.7.4 / commit 3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75; Honeycomb 0.5.0. Same isolated HOME/XDG/Git config and empty core.hooksPath as the preceding 34-case fixture. The probe reuses /private/tmp/hv-3x8.1-no-hooks-complete.nJKDwQ/probe.py's setup/run/check functions. Manual fixture config.yaml: issue_prefix: probe, sync.auto_import: true, sync.auto_flush: false; committed and pushed before its worktree creation. Expected refusal exit is 10; an initial harness assumption of exit 1 was corrected, without changing observed reason codes. No Hive application code/config changed; no full suite repeated because prior full locked check passed and all new verification is through disposable CLI lifecycle cases.

Upstream sync/default reference: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/blob/3956ebb8417414eba883e2446a4cefafa07d0b75/README.md. All results below are actual installed CLI behavior; illustrative diagrams explain those results. Parent hv-3x8.1 remains open for policy discussion.

title: Record: design conversation transcript (agent identity and bees)
description:
# Design conversation: agent identity and bees

Verbatim user/assistant dialogue from Claude Code session `5886da0d-8ce1-4f10-9909-8d0c8543094e` (2026-10-02), extracted by Pi (deepseek-flash) with the claude-session-introspection skill from the harness dialogue log. Tool calls, thinking, system reminders and background-task notifications are excluded. Turn markers are numbered `# [n] User` / `# [n] Assistant`; `##` headings inside turns are part of the messages. Turns 12–14 include earlier, abandoned wordings of the final request and one assistant reply from that abandoned attempt; they are kept as recorded. Second opinions from gpt-6-astra are summarised in the assistant turns, not reproduced. The conversation ends at the request that created this record.

# [1] User

i need to add identity to agents, this will allow bead audit trails to track the actor making changes

if you look through /Users/ct/dev/projects/millhouse.spool/spools/harnesses/plugins/millstrand-identity/README.md i had agents build this out before in another system, but i think it was a total mess and massively over complicated

help me walk through a way we could implement this in a way harnesses can use. It almost certainly needs to be a harness hook, like a claude code sessionStart hook (codex has the same) or pi which has a lower level typescript api

this gives usually gives us the model and effort, which we can use to drive env vars (if the harness lets us, which claude and pi do), and we can also pick up any environment variables set from outside, and finally we can inject the identity into the model's system prompt (helps insure it's clear and not just normal user prompt)

there are two ways an agent is launched, one is natively, e.g the desktop apps for claude/codex, the clis directly in a tty; the second is via some automation, e.g @scripts/beads-loop.ts which can much more easily set any needed env vars

for case 2, and agent might simply recieve NAME, MODEL, EFFORT, and then set its prompt. THis means we'd want some automation to mint the friendly identity first before passing it in
for case 1, the harness hook would need to mint the friendly identity (passing in model and effort from the hook if provided) and then pass this into the system prompt (and if the harness supports it, inject these as ENV vars so the agent doesn't need to keep typing them, as BD_ACTOR sets --actor automatically for example)

thoughts, you can use claude code session hooks as an example of how we'd build this

# [1] Assistant

I agree the old plugin was over-built: about 3,000 lines, a server registration callback, run references, Git workspace gates and conformance fixtures. Most of that existed only to keep identity state. If the name is derived from the session ID instead of stored, all of that state goes away.

## The core idea

Each harness hook is a thin adapter around one shared pure function. Automation only sets env vars. The hook always does the rendering.

title: Use shared Beads storage and publish explicit checkpoints
description: Retarget the existing unlanded shared-Beads policy implementation fab79f2 to the dedicated tracker migration epic hv-rgr. Keep one SQLite database in a permanent full tracker worktree per clone; publish JSONL/config only on its branch with default automatic export. Use authoritative local mise/direnv BEADS_DB and trusted per-checkout Codex shell environment settings instead of constructing a primary-checkout DB path. Reuse existing hook removal, quality hooks and Git merge driver. Preserve all stores and history, update publication/landing and reference docs, and verify fresh Codex CLI plus concurrent stub-feature worktrees. Original implementation and research evidence remain in notes and completed children; their main-publication design is superseded by the hv-rgr target. Do not implement identity functionality from hv-3x8 or land application changes without explicit authorization.
design:
Build the dedicated tracker design under hv-rgr in the existing worktree; use its child steps for setup, workflow and verification. One permanent full tracker checkout per clone owns the ignored SQLite runtime and tracked JSONL/config. Full checkout retains the existing relative Git merge driver and normal quality-hook tooling. Code branches retire the live tracked .beads snapshot, and the permanent tracker branch is never merged into main. Preserve every private store and capture consistent SQLite backups, including local history, before selecting the new authority. A configuration change does not migrate ignored DB files or protect them from worktree cleanup.

Use mise/direnv as the local environment authority. Prefer native Codex per-checkout shell_environment_policy.set over relying on the model to prefix BEADS_DB; settings hold a resolved absolute endpoint and do not evaluate shell expressions. Configure all linked checkouts from the same endpoint, without hardcoding machine paths in tracked files or overwriting unrelated user settings. Keep later Claude/Pi identity adapters separate, using their established dynamic environment channels. Do not assume the current root session or existing subagents refresh environment when files change; verify newly launched Codex CLI.

Read the supporting docs, spike findings and implementation beads. Claimed and synced **`hv-3x8.9.1`** for our design work; no code changes.

## Current interface baseline

| Interface | Recorded intent |
|---|---|
| `bee spawn <kind> <task-id>...` | Create a spawn request; don’t launch a process or claim its tasks. Return without waiting. |
| `bee status <spawn-id>` | Explain the request, linked-task readiness and execution outcome. Currently specified as Beads-only. |
| `colony wake` | Register a repository with the system-wide Colony; not start the daemon itself. Exact contract unfinished. |
| Close the spawn bead | End the request; Colony stops any running bee and releases unfinished claims. |

Daemon startup/shutdown, repository removal and runtime inspection commands are **not settled**.

## Constraints worth preserving

- **Request ≠ execution:** accepting a spawn does not mean a bee is running.
- **Repository ≠ worktree:** configuration, tracker selection and execution directory are separate concerns.
- Bees survive Colony restarts; replacement executions retain the request’s identity.
- All remaining open tasks must be ready before launch.
- `bee status` needs scheduling information, but currently cannot ask Colony. We must choose how Colony publishes that information—or revisit that restriction.
- Detached launches were demonstrated; complete adoption and descendant cleanup remain unverified.

Key references:
- `docs/agent-identity-scope.md:85` — configuration and command intent.
- `docs/harness-capabilities.md:35` — launch/recovery acceptance contract.
- `docs/beads-integration.md:29` — selected tracker endpoint, independent of execution cwd.

## Start with a concrete routing question

You’re in a feature worktree and request a bee for a task.

**Should the bee start in the canonical worktree and arrange its own working worktree, or inherit the caller’s worktree?**

My starting recommendation: **register repositories, not individual worktrees; launch from the canonical worktree, with worktree selection left to the bee’s workflow.** That keeps a queued request independent of a caller’s temporary checkout. An explicit execution-directory option should exist only if we have a concrete need.

## Bee

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `bee spawn <kind> <task-id>... [--cwd <dir>]` | Create a request; return its spawn ID and bee identity immediately. |
| `bee status <spawn-id>` | Show tasks, readiness, execution state and outcome. |

| `bee stop <spawn-id>` | Close the request; Colony stops its execution and releases unfinished claims. |

**Spawn and status are already planned.** List and stop are proposed conveniences. Stop would wrap request closure—not directly kill a PID.

The **spawn ID is the durable handle**, including before launch and across retries. A running process is not the handle.

## Colony

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `colony start` | Start the system-wide daemon. |
| `colony stop` | Stop the daemon, leaving detached bees alive. |
| `colony status` | Show daemon health, registered repositories and scheduling activity. |
| `colony wake` | Register/resume scheduling for the current repository. |
| `colony sleep` | Pause that repository’s scheduling; proposed to leave running bees alone. |

Only **wake’s registration intent** is established; these exact commands and semantics remain proposals. We may need a foreground `run` entry point for a service manager, but shouldn’t design a whole service-management framework.

- Human-readable output by default; `--json` for automation.
- Repository context and tracker selection stay separate from execution location.
- `bee spawn --cwd` controls **where the harness starts**, accepts any existing directory, and defaults to the canonical worktree.
- Logs remain outside Beads. Whether access needs `bee logs` / `colony logs` or just reported file locations is undecided.
- Status must distinguish recorded state from live observations—the current Beads-only requirement needs reconciliation.

I’d favour the **middle option**, not turning Bee into a generator of complete harness commands.

### Resolved recipe versus named kind

| Concern | Resolved recipe | Named kind |
|---|---|---|
| **Overrides** | `--config` is resolved entirely by Bee | Must convey the configuration source to Colony |
| **Queued work** | Keeps the settings chosen when requested | Configuration edits can change pending work |
| **Disposable files** | Original TOML can disappear afterward | Configuration must remain available at launch |
| **Request size/control** | Larger contract; more fields a producer can get wrong | Smaller request; Colony controls interpretation |
| **Colony complexity** | No configuration discovery or kind lookup | Owns discovery, lookup and configuration failures |
| **Changing pending work** | Requires changing/replacing the recipe | Editing configuration can affect subsequent launches |

The disposable-file benefit applies to the TOML itself—not scripts, skills or other files referenced by the recipe.

### The asynchronous failure concern

You’re right that more supplied fields create more opportunities for mistakes. But there are two different failure classes:

- **Malformed recipe:** Bee can catch this synchronously using a shared schema. Colony checks the same contract when reading Beads, because requests are external input.
- **Unusable invocation:** unavailable model, unsupported effort, bad extra flag, missing executable or credentials. These can fail at launch **under either design**. Looking up a kind name doesn’t make its configuration executable.

Keeping harness-specific argument construction in Colony reduces the first design’s brittleness: Bee expresses intent; Colony’s harness adapter translates it.

### When would Colony read configuration?

Only if we choose behavior that requires it:

- Resolve bee kinds at launch time.
- Read Colony-owned policy, such as concurrency limits.
- Re-evaluate configuration-dependent admission rules at launch.

Those policies don’t necessarily belong in the same file as bee definitions.

**My leaning:** Bee reads `bees.toml` and submits a resolved, declarative recipe. Colony validates and dispatches it through its harness adapter—without discovering or rereading bee-kind configuration.

### How it would work

1. **`colony wake`** loads canonical configuration: known kinds, launch templates and scheduling limits.
2. **Bee** reads configuration, selects a kind and applies request-specific overrides.
3. The spawn bead carries **kind + chosen parameter values + tasks + execution cwd**.

With your example, overriding `worker.harness` to `codex` changes the executable but leaves the **Claude-shaped argument template** attached to `worker`.

There are two coherent choices:

- **Harness fixed per kind:** your per-kind recipe arrangement works.
- **Harness overridable:** select the template by harness, independently of the kind.

```toml

harness = "claude"
model = "opus"
effort = "low"
min = 0
max = 10

executable = "claude"
args = ["--model", "{{ model }}", "--effort", "{{ effort }}", "--yolo"]
```

*Illustrative configuration syntax, not a validated harness invocation.*

Here, **kind controls defaults and scheduling; harness controls invocation syntax**. Multiple kinds can share the same harness template.

Keep executable and argument tokens separate rather than rendering a shell command string. That avoids making quoting, spaces and shell interpretation part of your configuration language.

Your scout example also references `effort` without defining it. Template validation should expose that missing value, rather than silently producing an empty argument.

- **Same file does not mean same snapshot.** Colony reads on wake; Bee might read after an edit. A new kind therefore needs that explicit configuration-update operation before Colony can execute it.

- **Priority:** use the highest urgency among linked tasks—P0 before P1. BV provides scores, but its tested triage output is bounded to ten recommendations, so it isn’t yet a complete queue-ordering interface. We’ll investigate that integration rather than invent another ranking system.
- **Templates:** **Handlebars** looks suitable: established library, strict missing-field handling and disabled HTML escaping. Its compilation is lazy, so we must explicitly validate template syntax when loading configuration—not accidentally defer malformed syntax until launch.
- **Overrides:** transient; every wake reloads canonical configuration. No override recovery exception.
- **Limits:** drop `min`; retain non-preemptive maximums.

### One correction to #4

A **closed spawn bead still exists**. On waking:

- Closed request, no surviving execution → nothing to launch.
- Closed request, surviving execution → earlier policy says stop that execution and release its unfinished claims.

Ignoring closed requests entirely would miss the second case. **I recommend reconciliation handles it on wake; no background polling while asleep.**

Next step is to define the command/flag/help surface in `cli.ts` before implementing dispatch, scheduling or storage. That will give us something concrete to use while refining registration and status.

title: Spike: harness identity hook contracts (Claude Code, Codex, Pi)
description:
scent needs exact, verified contracts for each harness's session-start integration. Verify against installed versions (record versions) rather than docs alone.

Per harness, establish:
- Hook/extension entry point and when it fires (startup, resume, clear, compact; subagent start).
- Payload fields: session id, model, effort/thinking level. Known so far: Codex SessionStart input is {session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, model, permission_mode, source} and output accepts only hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (vendored codex-rs/hooks/src/schema.rs); Claude effort availability is unknown.
- Session id stability across resume, fork, clear and compact.
- Env injection: Claude CLAUDE_ENV_FILE semantics (quoting, whether Task subagents share it or run hooks), Pi process.env mutation reaching tool subprocesses, Codex (none expected).
- Prompt injection: additionalContext placement (system reminder vs developer message), Pi before_agent_start systemPrompt.
- Whether hook processes inherit the harness env (needed to read HIVE_AGENT_*).

Use disposable sessions; no model work beyond what is needed to observe behaviour.
design: Research-only spike in .worktrees/spike--hv-3x8.2: verify installed Claude Code, Codex, and Pi using isolated temporary configs/sessions and sentinel hook/extension probes; corroborate lifecycle and injection behavior with installed or version-matched source, explicitly distinguish runtime observations from source-backed and unresolved claims. Record sanitized samples and a capability matrix in bead notes; call out scent design gaps on parent epic. No production code or unrelated beads.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Capability matrix (entry point, payload fields, env injection, prompt injection, session id stability) per harness recorded in notes with versions
- [x] Sample payloads captured for each harness
- [x] Open gaps that change the scent design called out on the epic
notes:
## Verified harness identity contracts — hv-3x8.2

Research-only spike; no production modules, dependencies or repository docs added. Probed disposable configs/sessions and sentinels on 2026-10-02/03 UTC. O = observed on installed harness; S = inspected installed bundle or version-matched source; U = not live-verified. Source-backed lifecycle results are NOT represented as runtime captures.

Versions/provenance:
- Claude Code `2.1.287 (Claude Code)` (`claude --version` at probe start), native binary `/Users/ct/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.287`; bundled JS inspected via strings. All captured conversation/subagent records report version 2.1.287. The default CLI auto-updated to 2.1.288 by review time; that release is NOT covered by this matrix. Reproduce using the pinned 2.1.287 binary, whose --version was rechecked. Not a docs-only result.
- Codex `codex-cli 0.160.0` (`codex --version`). Source tag `rust-v0.160.0`, tag object `79b1b666f2e8551f8abbbca34957227f67f3f553`, commit `a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc`, fetched read-only through GitHub API. Existing vendor HEAD `e597169e9a783156e50ae9765d891a3dd74df064` is older and omits `fork`; it must NOT be used as the installed contract.
- Pi `1.0.0` (`pi --version`), installed `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` at `/Users/ct/.pi/agent/install/releases/1.0.0/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. Agents checkout's 0.99.1 package is not the installed release.

### Capability matrix

| Capability | Claude Code 2.1.287 | Codex 0.160.0 | Pi 1.0.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry point | Command hook in settings/plugin `hooks.SessionStart`; JSON stdin/stdout (O). | Command hook in `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json` (`{"hooks":{...}}`); JSON stdin/stdout (O). Inline config/plugin sources also supported (S). | TS extension `pi.on("session_start", (event, ctx) => ...)`, loaded with `-e` or normal extension discovery (O/S). No JSON stdin hook. |
| Startup/resume/fork | SessionStart source `startup`/`resume`/`fork` observed. Resume same UUID; fork new UUID (O). | SessionStart source `startup`/`resume`/`fork` observed on first turn. Resume same root id; fork new root id (O). Hook dispatch is deferred until an agent turn, not just process launch (S). | Startup event; runtime switch emits `session_shutdown` then `session_start` reason `resume`/`fork`; same id on resume, new id on fork (O). Initial disposable RPC process reported startup; use ctx id, not reason alone, to resolve identity. |
| Clear/new | SessionEnd `clear`, rotates session UUID, then SessionStart `clear` (S; live TUI capture unavailable). | InitialHistory::Cleared creates a new root thread/session id and queues SessionStart `clear` (S; live TUI unavailable). | `/new` / RPC `new_session` is the clear-equivalent: shutdown/start reason `new`, new id (O). No core `/clear`. |
| Compaction | Reuses current session; SessionStart `compact` after compaction, in addition to compact hooks (S; live unavailable). | Replaces history in same Session; queues SessionStart `compact` for next dispatch, no identity rotation (S; live unavailable). | `session_before_compact` -> `session_compact`; same id; NO `session_start` (O). |
| Subagent start | Agent tool (formerly Task) emits `SubagentStart`, not a fresh root SessionStart. `session_id` remains parent; separate `agent_id`, `agent_type`; transcript_path is parent (O). | ThreadSpawn from `collaborationspawn_agent` emits `SubagentStart`, not SessionStart. `session_id` is ROOT identity; `agent_id` is child thread; transcript_path is child (O/S). Internal/synthetic subagents skipped (S). | No core subagent event. Separate child Pi process gets its own startup event/id and inherits parent env (O). Existing agents extension spawns such processes (S; plugin itself not live-tested). |
| Model/effort | SessionStart model optional (S) and ABSENT under --model haiku, settings pin, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, --effort low (O). Effort absent at SessionStart; optional model-gated field on tool-context hooks (S), not observed on Haiku. Compact callsite supplies model (S). | SessionStart includes resolved `model`; no effort/thinking field (O/S). transcript_path nullable by schema (S). | `ctx.model?.provider/id`, `ctx.thinkingLevel` (optional by types); reasoning model high, non-reasoning off; high->low change observed (O/S). Not event payload fields. |
| Environment injection | `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` in SessionStart points to per-session hook shell script. Exports reach subsequent main AND subagent Bash calls; single-quoted special characters round-trip (O). Not a parent process.env mutation or a SubagentStart env channel. | No env/env-file output channel in hook schema (S). Static handler env affects hook process only (S). Launcher env still inherited (O). Native scent needs explicit --actor prompt guidance. | Mutation of process.env at session_start reaches pi.exec, model bash, RPC bash and a separately spawned Pi process (O). |
| Prompt injection | `{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"SessionStart",additionalContext:"..."}}` produces hook_additional_context attachment before user prompt (O). Bundle maps it into meta role=user message wrapped by system-reminder, NOT a true system/developer role (S; provider body not captured). | Same output channel; separate role=developer input_text message, tagged hooks.additional_context, observed in rollout (O/S). | Stable composable identity: return `{systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + identity}` on every before_agent_start; later handlers receive the composed prompt. Leading system prompt (provider adapter rendered developer for fake OpenAI model), not a reminder attachment (O; composition verified in the follow-up below). |
| Parent env inheritance | HIVE_AGENT_NAME/SESSION/PARENT sentinels visible in SessionStart, SubagentStart, main Bash and subagent Bash (O). | HIVE_AGENT_NAME/SESSION/PARENT sentinels visible in SubagentStart hook; name also in all captured root events (O). Command runner inherits env + configured additions (S). | HIVE_AGENT_* sentinels in extension and subprocesses; parent-only mutation inherited by separate child (O). |

### Exact boundaries and implications

Claude:
- Observed minimal SessionStart keys are `session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, source`. Resume/fork add `seconds_since_last_response, context_tokens, prompt_cache_likely_expired, estimated_cache_write_usd`. Missing model/effort means ABSENT, not JSON null. Schema's optional fields are not startup guarantees.
- SessionStart output hookEventName is case-sensitive. Lowercase `sessionstart` produced a non-blocking hook error and dropped context; exact `SessionStart` worked.
- SessionStart env file is `session-env/<sid>/sessionstart-hook-N.sh`; subsequent hook processes (including SubagentStart) did NOT receive CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. Script contents are collected and applied by Bash execution (S); they do not prove arbitrary harness subprocess env mutation. Quote generated values as shell data. Single-quoted spaces, double quotes, literal $HOME, backticks and a backslash round-tripped byte-for-byte in both main and subagent Bash (see env snapshots). Unquoted expansion was not live-tested.
- Native Agent subagents share parent-session env exports. Root-session-only identity resolution cannot give each native subagent its own exported actor; a SubagentStart prompt may use agent_id, but that does not change per-session shell env. Separate nested CLI processes are different from native subagents.
- `--init-only` is zero-model startup probe, but reports source startup even with --resume/--fork-session. Real -p resume/fork probes were required; do not use init-only to infer lifecycle sources.

Codex:
- Exact SessionStart keys are `session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, model, permission_mode, source`; no turn_id. SubagentStart adds turn_id/agent_id/agent_type. Root session_id deliberately shared by descendant threads in 0.160.0, not a unique child conversation id.
- Output wire is camelCase. SessionStart universal keys also allow continue/stopReason/suppressOutput/systemMessage; hookSpecificOutput carries hookEventName/additionalContext. No env/environment key. Inheritance alone cannot bind an HIVE_AGENT_SESSION in native Codex tools; do not claim prompt guidance exports it.
- Observed exec hook trust gating: without `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, hooks were skipped with warnings. Bypass was used only with disposable probe-owned hooks; production installation/launch must make an explicit trust decision.
- Initial subagent-negative probe had SubagentStart unregistered. Corrected registration DID fire it. Collaboration subagents are NOT a blind spot; only internal/synthetic sources are skipped (S). Earlier vendor-based claims are superseded.

Pi:
- session_start event has `{type,reason,previousSessionFile?}`; session id/model/thinking come from ctx, not JSON stdin. New/resume/fork replacement in RPC emitted session_start/resources_discover TWICE; confirmed double rebind callsites in installed RPC/core. Make identity resolution idempotent by current session id; do not infer two sessions from two callbacks. This duplication claim is RPC-specific, not proven for TUI.
- before_agent_start input has prompt, images?, readonly systemPrompt, mutable systemPromptOptions. Returning systemPrompt replaces the complete prompt for that run; append/preserve prior text. Override observed on every provider request in a tool loop, absent from persisted JSONL and compaction summary request. Reinject on each agent run. model_select and thinking_level_select can refresh best-effort metadata after startup (S; thinking change O).
- Built-in model Bash gets PI_SESSION_ID/PI_SESSION_FILE/PI_PROVIDER/PI_MODEL/PI_REASONING_LEVEL resolved per call. RPC/user Bash did not receive those automatic session vars, but DID receive process.env mutations. Do not conflate those paths.
- Pi probe used a local canned OpenAI-compatible provider; zero real-model work for its lifecycle, compaction, prompt or tool-env tests.

Actual command probes: claude --init-only; claude -p "Reply with exactly OK" --model haiku --max-turns 1; same with --resume <id> and --fork-session; one main + Agent Bash env readback.
- Bundle citations use LF/vimgrep line numbers (`rg -n`), not Python splitlines(), which additionally counts embedded Unicode separators (e.g. zQr is LF line 345774, splitlines index 349742). `/tmp/hv-3x8.2-claude-strings.txt:345774`: randomUUID import + zQr rotates identity; `:368017` B_r clear calls SessionEnd clear, zQr({setCurrentAsParent:true}), then H5 clear. `:354447` and `:354451` post-compact H5 uses same session. `:354491` QIr builds SessionStart input. `:355731` hook_additional_context mapper -> Re(cl(...),isMeta); `:355618` Re constructor role=user; `:345892` system-reminder constants; `:353105` env script reader. - Matched Codex source: https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.160.0 . `codex-rs/hooks/src/schema.rs:386` SessionStart output, `:499` SessionStart input; `events/session_start.rs:25` source enum. `codex-rs/core/src/session/session.rs:853` new/clear/fork generate thread ids, `:895` root session id resolution, `:1905` source selection; `codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs:4104` same-session history replacement and `:4212` queues compact. `codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs:129` deferred dispatch + child mapping; `:849` context recording. Downloaded copies `/tmp/hv-3x8.2-codex/evidence/source-0.160.0/REF.txt:1`; old vendor is explicitly superseded.

PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR isolated; pi --mode rpc --no-extensions -e probe-extension.ts --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-themes --no-context-files --session-dir <temp> --model probe/probe-model --thinking high --offline. - Installed Pi package: `dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:213` ctx, `:547` session events, `:693` before_agent_start, `:1082` output; `dist/core/tools/bash.js:135` env resolution. `dist/core/agent-session-runtime.js:120` rebind and `dist/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.js:338,477,484` repeat binding explain duplicate starts. Source filenames are relative to the exact installed package recorded above.

### Remaining design gaps (call out on epic)

1. New UUID on clear/new AND fork: inherited HIVE_AGENT_SESSION mismatch also occurs during same-process new/clear/fork, not just nested children. Decide whether HIVE_AGENT_PARENT should describe all identity transitions or only actual spawning; session reason/previous file can distinguish Pi transitions. Do not label every mismatch a nested process by assumption.
2. Native subagent identity: Claude and Codex lifecycle session_id is parent/root, with separate agent_id. Claude env-file scope is shared; Codex has no dynamic env output channel. ct selected explicit actor guidance for native Claude and Codex subagents, using the distinct agent_id for child identity and --actor to override inherited parent attribution. Primary Claude and Pi retain environment-based attribution. See the current decision and evidence below. Colony-launched separate CLIs remain in scope; retiring native definitions does not remove harness-native tools.
3. Best-effort metadata: Claude startup model absent and effort unavailable; Codex effort absent. Do not require values or invent fallbacks; launcher metadata can be retained where known. Pi context is richer but needs refresh on model/thinking changes.
4. Lifecycle implementation details: Pi supports stable, composable identity by appending to the current system prompt on every before_agent_start; this is normal extension behavior, not an unresolved persistence concern (ct clarification and runtime follow-up below). Pi compact does not fire session_start. RPC duplicate session-start handling must still be idempotent. Claude/Codex use compact sources, with source-backed rather than live evidence in this spike.
5. Codex native attribution relies on explicit --actor guidance, not env export. Nested CLI parent-link inference is incomplete when a native Codex parent cannot bind/export HIVE_AGENT_SESSION. ## Pi prompt composition clarification — ct, 2026-10-03

Pi prompt persistence is not an unresolved identity limitation. Each before_agent_start handler reads the current composed event.systemPrompt and appends its own contribution. The next handler sees that returned prompt. Repeating the same composition on each agent run maintains stable identity and preserves other extensions; the per-run return value is normal API mechanics, not evidence that identity disappears between turns. A renderer that owns the base prompt runs before appenders.

Verified against installed Pi 1.0.0: extensions/runner.js:1115-1160 renders the current options for each handler and applies each returned systemPrompt as the next forceSystemPrompt. agent-session.js:1555 starts each run from base options; :1314 projects the override across provider requests and :1373 clears run options on completion. This does not undermine stable per-run composition. Compaction uses its own prompt, as originally recorded; the identity contribution is re-established for subsequent agent runs.

Focused runtime evidence: node /tmp/hive-pi-prompt-composition.mjs exercised the actual installed ExtensionRunner.emitBeforeAgentStart and buildSystemPrompt with two probe handlers across three independent calls. All 29 assertions passed: the second handler saw the first contribution; the base prompt and both contributions survived in order; exactly one copy of each contribution appeared; outputs were identical across runs; caller base options were unchanged. This probes the installed runner with minimal context, not a new full CLI/provider lifecycle test. Earlier spike provider captures remain the evidence for tool-loop requests.

Practical reference: /Users/ct/dev/projects/agents/pi/extensions/system-prompt/index.ts:301-331 rebuilds the owned prompt with cached identity every before_agent_start; package.json loads this renderer first. Downstream extensions compose after it. The existing cross-extension integration test was inspected as an example, not newly executed. That checkout declares Pi 0.99.1 dependencies; installed-runner verification used Pi 1.0.0. No changes to the agents repository or Hive production code.

The original every-run append guidance was correct. Calling it a design gap, and the later spoken phrase “the prompt is temporary,” overstated the limitation. ct considers this normal composition pattern sufficient; no extra prompt-persistence mechanism is requested. RPC duplicate session-start callbacks and session ancestry semantics remain separate findings.

- Separately launched CLI processes, including colony bees, retain launcher-provided environment support. Identity attribution support for native subagents does not make them colony-managed spawn beads.
