Existing owned executions still have their attempt records; the CLI must expose that they can outlive registration. Re-add/wake can reconcile them without duplicate launch.
- Per-worktree capacity uses the worktree containing the recorded launch cwd, or canonicalized external cwd when it is not in a worktree. Capture that bucket at dispatch; do not chase later process chdir or automatically-created worktrees. Canonical-default launches therefore share the canonical bucket. Scope the colony-wide total per registered repository; a server-global budget is not required initially.
- BV investigation must not stall the build. Prefer a verified complete score source for eligible task IDs and aggregate by best ranked linked task within a native-priority tier. Known triage output can be top-10 only. If no complete contract is available, use explicitly documented FIFO (request creation time, then ID) within the priority tier, expose that mode, and retain the limitation in the final report. Do not treat missing BV scores as proof of lowest rank or silently change a configured ranking mode after an error.

Read this epic before every child task. Work only inside this prototype subtree: select an unblocked open leaf task, inspect it, claim with your harness actor and owner ct, sync, implement in the dedicated worktree, verify, append evidence, close and sync. Parent ownership is not a child claim. Respect existing reservations. Close a feature only when its children and feature-level smoke outcomes are complete, then continue to the next feature. Do not stop just because the first demo works, and do not select unrelated ready work outside this subtree.

All prototype work is AFK-eligible: no hitl label or human assignment gates are planned. Missing product details should be resolved conservatively under this directive, with a recorded prototype decision, rather than sent back as a new grilling round. Genuine external blockers, tracker sync conflicts, unsafe process ownership, missing credentials or new destructive scope still require an honest stop/report; autonomy is not permission to force them. title: honeycomb: move wk wrapper behaviour into the engine (simplify; focus follows humans, never agents)
description:
Move worktree lifecycle behaviour out of the Nushell `wk` wrapper (`lib/honeycomb/nu/honeycomb/`, ~475 lines) into the honeycomb engine, leaving the shell layer as a thin alias whose only irreducible job is changing the calling shell's cwd.

This is a simplification. `wk` works well today; the goal is to move the same behaviour into TypeScript and delete duplication, not to add new safety machinery.

## What moves

- Post-create setup and its rollback (today: wrapper runs the script, then rolls back via the `HONEYCOMB_INTERNAL_ROLLBACK` backdoor and a raw `git branch -f`).
- tmux open/switch/close and session naming (already emitted as `session.name`).
- The fzf worktree picker.
- `--self` resolution and human status lines.

The pool-full recycle picker already exists in the engine (`pickFullPoolSlot`); the wrapper only reimplemented it because it calls `--json`. The shim will call human mode, so it disappears for free.

## Focus follows the human, never the agent

One flag, `--interactive`, passed only by `wk`:

- **With it**: `add` opens and focuses the worktree's multiplexer session (or tells the shell to `cd` when not in a multiplexer); `remove`/`finish` close sessions for removed worktrees and send the shell to the canonical root if it was inside one.
- **Without it** (agents, scripts): no multiplexer calls and no cd directive at all. An agent can't steal focus or kill a session because it never touches sessions.

Terminal detection is deliberately not used: agents run inside the user's tmux panes and can have a PTY.

## Decisions

- `add` always runs setup in the engine. No deferred mode. `post_create_script_path` stays in JSON as always `null`.
- Multiplexer support is a small injected service (tmux first) so another multiplexer with a similar API could replace it.
- Shell cwd handoff: the engine writes a directory path to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`.
- `remove --self` is a boolean (the worktree containing `--cwd`).
- JSON changes are additive only.

## End state

`mod.nu` is a ~30-line shim; `tmux.nu` is deleted.

title: honeycomb: HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE shell cwd handoff
description:
Implement the `HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE` directive exactly as specified in the spec task.

## Scope

- Add a directive-file operation behind an injected service (`WorkspaceFiles` has none today, `src/services.ts`).
